schema_notes: Each company entry is ground truth for eval/run_eval.ts to compare pipeline output against.

Sourcing rule: every cited `source_url` is a company website page, an official registry, an official press release, or a news article that did its own original reporting. Aggregator/directory pages (Crunchbase, PitchBook, LinkedIn, Tracxn, Dealroom, Sacra, Seedtable, CB Insights, etc.) were used only to FIND candidate facts and leads during research — never as the cited source for a value here.
Never seeded from AlphaMap's own database — built independently so comparing against it is meaningful.

confidence per field: 'verified' (2+ independent primary/direct-reporting sources agree, or one lead-investor/company-direct source), 'likely' (one credible direct-reporting source, not independently corroborated), 'unknown' (no primary source found, or sources conflict with no way to resolve). Fields marked 'unknown' are excluded from precision/coverage scoring, not guessed.
hard_case_tags follow the v2 spec's categories (Section 6 / issue 13): common_name, non_us, rebrand_domain_change, series_a_start, stealth_no_data, went_public.

companies.production_bug_notes: AlphaMap's live DB showed 'Growth (Jun 2026)' and 'Series D (Apr 2026)' as two $200M/$2.3B rows and flagged them for merging as a duplicate. Verified research shows the REAL Series D was Sept 2025 (not Apr 2026) at a ~$1B valuation, and the Jun 2026 round is a genuinely separate, later, third $200M raise at $2.3B. The production data's 'Apr 2026' date for 'Series D' matches no real event found — it appears to be a hallucinated/mis-dated entry, not a legitimate duplicate of the June round. The correct fix is 6 distinct rounds with correct dates, not a 2-into-1 merge.

companies.name: Fresha
companies.rebrand_notes: Launched 2015 as 'Shedul'/'Shedul.com', originally Dubai-based; rebranded to 'Fresha' in 2020 and now headquartered in London. A v2 entity/domain check must not treat pre-2020 Shedul-era sources as a different company, must not let a stale 'shedul.com' domain reference fail domain verification against the current fresha.com, and must get the CURRENT (London) HQ right rather than the historical (Dubai) one when both appear across sources from different years.

This is the round that pushed Fresha to unicorn status, widely covered independently by multiple outlets on 2026-05-22 — highest-confidence round in this set alongside the Series A and Series C.

funding_rounds_excluded_unknown.notes: Reported as a 'Series C Plus' top-up by aggregator pages only; no primary source found in this pass. Excluded from scoring. A real test case for v2's round-dedup logic once a primary source is found: is this a distinct round, or should it merge with the June 2021 Series C above?

total_raised_usd_reported.notes: Aggregator-reported aggregate (not independently confirmed); do not use as a scoring target for 'Total Raised' — compare against total_raised_usd_computed_from_verified_rounds instead.

companies.total_raised_discrepancy_notes: The aggregator-reported total ($285M) exceeds the sum of rounds we could verify to a primary source ($206M: 6M+20M+100M+80M). This is a realistic, common gap between a headline aggregate and an itemized round list, made of some combination of: the unverified $52.5M 'Series C Plus' tranche above, and/or other undisclosed rounds. v2's 'never compute Total Raised from a model-returned total' rule (issue 5) should recompute from whichever individual rounds it actually stored — which will legitimately read LOWER than some press-reported aggregates until every round is independently itemized, and that's correct behavior, not a bug.

employee_count.notes: LinkedIn's self-reported bucket (201-500), LinkedIn's own 'people' count (~728), and third-party aggregators (500/718/916) all disagree by up to 2x depending on collection date through 2026 — and LinkedIn itself is excluded as a citable source under this golden set's sourcing rule. No primary (company-stated) headcount figure was found in this pass. Left unknown rather than picking a number.

companies.production_bug_notes: AlphaMap's live DB showed 140,000 employees — wrong by 2-3 orders of magnitude against every candidate figure found (the real range is in the low hundreds to ~900s). Likely root cause: Fresha is independently reported to be 'operating at more than $140 million in revenue run-rate as of May 2026' (ARR) — the production pipeline most plausibly confused this $140M ARR figure with an employee count (a field-confusion/unit bug), rather than genuinely mis-searching for headcount. Worth checking whether v1's extraction prompt or v2's schema could cross-contaminate an ARR figure into employee_count under the wrong conditions.
